title: Tenant invocation patterns mart and sparse storage strategy
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: build a compact, query-efficient tenant-level invocation mart that captures per-tenant and per-route invocation patterns while minimizing storage and scan costs. This ticket covers the model, materialization strategy, compaction/retention policies, and the migration plan to switch Console dashboards and SLO pipelines over to the new mart.

Background: current console slices rely on high-cardinality event tables and ad-hoc sessionized views which are expensive for large tenants and slow for alerting. We need a curated mart that: (1) supports fast per-tenant rollups for weekly/daily/hourly queries, (2) stores sparse metrics efficiently for long-tail tenants, and (3) provides a small dense index for top tenants to power low-latency dashboards.

Design highlights:
- Primary mart: tenant_invocation_patterns_mart (BigQuery) with partitioning by date (DAY) and clustering on tenant_id, route_id.
- Sparse storage technique: store per-tenant deltas using a compact row format for non-zero metrics (invocations, avg_latency_ms, error_count, token_count). Long-tail tenants with <100 invocations/day are encoded as compressed rows with an encoding_type flag to avoid repeated empty columns.
- Dense index: tenant_top_index table materialized daily for tenants in top-1k by monthly invocation volume; this table is denormalized for dashboard queries and kept in a single-day partition for fast lookups.
- Micro-aggregates: maintain hourly_rollups and daily_rollups derived from event stream (Beam job) with idempotent keys to enable safe retries.
- Retention & compaction: keep raw sparse rows for 180 days, compact monthly into a monthly_summary table with one row per tenant-month. Compaction runs as a backfill batch using a Dataflow job referenced below.
- SCD handling: workspace and tenant dimensions follow SCD-2 with effective_from/effective_to to capture workspace name/owner changes; dimension snapshots materialized weekly to limit join costs.

Schema preview (columns):
- tenant_id
- route_id
- window_start_date
- encoding_type (dense|sparse)
- invocation_count
- avg_latency_ms
- p95_latency_ms
- error_count
- token_count_total
- sample_invocation_examples (JSON string pointer)
- last_updated_ts

Materialization & pipeline:
1) Streaming ingestion: Beam job consumes Console callstream (pub/sub) and writes hourly_rollups into BigQuery staging tables using insertId dedup.
2) Daily materializer: Airflow DAG runs daily to fold hourly_rollups into tenant_invocation_patterns_mart partition for that date. Uses MERGE for idempotency.
3) Compaction job: monthly Dataflow/Spark job compacts old sparse rows into monthly_summary and deletes rows older than 180 days.

Backfill plan: start with a two-week shadow run and parallel-read test from existing sessionized views. After queries match within tolerance, run full backfill for last 12 months in rate-limited batches. Backfill tracked via backfill_job_id in job metadata.

Migration strategy:
- Phase 1 (shadow): populate mart and run Console dashboards/queries against both old and new sources, compare latency and cost.
- Phase 2 (canary): switch a subset of tenants (low-volume) to read-from-mart only for dashboards and alerts.
- Phase 3 (cutover): gradual routing of traffic for remaining tenants with a fallback route to old views for 7 days.

Testing & validation:
- Unit tests for Beam transforms and MERGE logic.
- Integration validation: nightly checksum job to compare aggregates to canonical callstream totals.
- Cost validation: query cost regression threshold (daily avg query cost must be <= 60% of current baseline for equivalent queries).

Ownership & runbook:
- Data owner: Marcus Li.
- Oncall escalation: analytics-sre on PagerDuty.
- Runbook includes steps to pause compaction, roll back MERGE DAG, and re-run re-synchronization.

notes: Tradeoff: sparse encoding reduces storage but increases decode work in some ad-hoc SQLs; mitigated by providing helper UDFs and a dense index for common high-volume tenants.
Decision: BigQuery chosen for zero-ops and existing console analytics workflows; evaluated Delta Lake but rejected due to current infra investments and query SLAs.
Follow-up: consider adding precomputed p99 for top tenants if alert noise persists after rollout.
